note: Owner confirmed the G2-01 probe on 2026-10-14 (valid; both finder requests Z.AI with reported model z-ai/glm-5.3, reported reasoning tokens and cost; no inline reasoning) and asked to run the series in sealed order, stopping only at sealed stops.
counter delta exceeds the reported $0.065366 by $0.076530 (unreported spend, e.g. grading or an aborted request)

findings.description: This script lacks the localhost/127.0.0.1 URL check and the service-role key shape check (`KEY.count('.') == 2 or KEY.startswith('sb_secret_')`) that its sibling has, so it can run against a local stack or with an anon key and produce confusing 403s.
findings.suggestion: Copy the two extra guards from prod-result-dimensions.py for consistency between the pair.

findings.description: Matching uses `j["id"][:8] not in WANTED`, but the docstring advertises 'any job-id prefixes'; a user passing a full UUID silently matches nothing and the script reports all jobs missing.
findings.suggestion: Either truncate each argument to 8 chars or compare with `j["id"].startswith(w)` and document the accepted prefix length.

findings.description: The signed-URL call and the download loop are not wrapped in the error handling the jobs query gets. On an HTTPError the traceback prints the failing request URL — for the download that includes the signed-URL token (300 s TTL, low risk, but the file's own contract says nothing signed should be logged) — and for `api()` failures the user gets a raw stack trace instead of the script's die() style.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the sign and download calls in try/except like the jobs query, catching HTTPError/URLError and reporting via die() or a per-job warning without echoing the URL.

findings.description: `missing` is computed by listing the output directory and matching filename prefixes, so a leftover file from a previous run (or from a different WANTED set) satisfies the check and suppresses the 'NOT found in the jobs table' message incorrectly.
findings.suggestion: Track the matched prefixes during the loop (e.g. `matched = {short for j in jobs if ...}`) and compute `missing = [w for w in WANTED if w not in matched]`.

findings.description: The script claims it 'never fetches a whole image', but urllib will happily read a 200 response where the server ignored the Range header; `raw = r.read()` then downloads the entire object, so the safety contract is unenforced. Also, 2048 bytes is often too small for phone JPEGs whose EXIF (with embedded thumbnail) precedes the SOF marker, causing them to fall into 'header not recognised' — and the final CONFIRMED verdict is printed even when `unreadable > 0`, so systematic false-unreadables can silently skew the census conclusion.
findings.suggestion: Check `r.status == 206` (or cap the read, e.g. `r.read(32768)`), increase the range to 16–32 KiB, and only print CONFIRMED when `unreadable == 0` (otherwise flag the conclusion as provisional).

findings.description: The JPEG byte scanner doesn't handle 0xFF padding followed by 0x00 or TEM (0x01), and a literal 0xFF marker byte falls into the length-skip branch with a garbage length, desynchronizing the scan. Fine for well-formed files, but the census conclusion rests on this parser.
findings.suggestion: Skip 0xFF fill bytes and marker 0x01 explicitly, and bail out of the loop when the segment length read would take `i` past the buffer instead of continuing with garbage.

findings.description: The key guard here only rejects angle-bracket placeholders, while the sibling script `prod-result-dimensions.py` also rejects anon/publishable keys by shape. A wrong key type produces a confusing PostgREST error rather than a clear one.
findings.suggestion: Copy the `KEY.count('.') == 2 or KEY.startswith('sb_secret_')` shape check from prod-result-dimensions.py for consistency.

findings.description: Two jobs sharing an 8-character id prefix both write `{short}-{date}.png`; the second silently overwrites the first while `found` counts both, so the reported totals and files on disk can disagree.
findings.suggestion: Include more of the job id (or a collision check) in the destination filename.

findings.description: The `missing` check re-derives matches from `os.listdir(OUT)` filename prefixes. A stale file from a previous run (or any coincidentally-prefixed file) suppresses the warning even when the current run saved nothing, and the 'NOT found in the jobs table' message mis-describes failures that are actually prefix mismatches.
findings.suggestion: Track matched prefixes during the loop (`matched = {short for j in jobs if ...}`) and compute `missing = [w for w in WANTED if w not in matched]` instead of scanning the output directory.

findings.description: Header parsers can raise instead of returning None: the PNG branch does `struct.unpack('>II', raw[16:24])` without a length check (a short ranged response crashes the census loop with struct.error), and the JPEG scanner treats 0xFF fill bytes as a length-bearing marker, desyncing the scan. Since the whole loop has no try/except around parsing, one malformed object aborts the entire census.
findings.suggestion: Validate `len(raw) >= 24` before the PNG unpack, handle JPEG 0xFF fill bytes, and wrap the `dimensions()` call in the existing unreadable path so a parse failure counts as unreadable rather than crashing.

findings.description: The docstring's contract — 'never fetches a whole image' — is not enforced. The ranged GET sends `Range: bytes=0-2047` but never checks `r.status == 206` or truncates the read; a server/proxy that ignores Range means `r.read()` downloads every full-size image.
findings.suggestion: Check `r.status == 206` (or cap the read to 2048 bytes) and treat a full-body 200 as an error/unknown rather than proceeding.

findings.description: The '=> CONFIRMED: no production job has ever exercised Cloud AI at a real phone's resolution' verdict fires whenever `downscaled == 0 and passed > 0`, even if many jobs were unreadable. Since this output is intended as evidence for S-17, an unqualified confirmation with a blind spot is misleading.
findings.suggestion: Gate the CONFIRMED message on `unreadable == 0`, or include the unreadable count in the message (e.g. 'confirmed for N readable of M jobs').

findings.description: Imports use relative paths into ../../src/ rather than the repo's @/* alias convention (same in browser-stats.ts, desktop-stats.ts, harness.ts). If tsx resolves the tsconfig paths, the alias should be used; if not, a note is warranted so the relative paths aren't 'fixed' into breakage later.
findings.suggestion: Switch to @/lib/engines/... imports if tsx honors tsconfig paths, otherwise add a one-line comment in harness.ts explaining why relative paths are required.

findings.description: The STAT_FIELDS/PERCENTILES/bin-rounding comparison and the params-check block are duplicated nearly verbatim in desktop-stats.ts's compare(). The two scripts already share harness.ts; if the two parity definitions drift, the auditability these scripts exist to provide silently degrades.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared compareStats(offline, next) helper (alongside STAT_FIELDS and the tolerance constants) into harness.ts and use it from both scripts.

findings.description: Captions interpolate record['prediction_id'], entry['path'], and the size-mismatch note into HTML without html.escape, while figure() escapes src. All inputs are local maintainer-generated files so the blast radius is nil, but escaping is applied inconsistently within the same page.
findings.suggestion: html.escape the caption strings built in build_photo, or route all caption text through a helper that escapes.

findings.description: In compare(), `const a = base[id]` is used without a check while the download side is checked. With --baseline <older-file> (the reader explicitly supports the older bare { id: stats } shape) a missing id throws a TypeError instead of the documented clean exit 1. Additionally, the module-level photo-loading loop runs before argument handling, so even a pure --compare of two JSON files requires all licensed inputs to be present on disk.
findings.suggestion: Guard `if (!a)` with the same exit-1 message as the download side, and skip loading/hashing the photo inputs when --compare is given.

findings.description: The prediction polling loop has no timeout backstop and no poll.ok check: a prediction stuck in a non-terminal state, a non-2xx poll whose body parses to a prediction without a terminal status, or a fetch that keeps failing will spin forever. This matches the repo's explicit red flag about waits on external services without a timeout covering every non-terminal state.
findings.suggestion: Cap the loop (e.g. 10 minutes), check poll.ok, and exit non-zero naming the prediction id and its manual-cancel URL.

findings.description: A transient network error or HTTP error during polling throws an unhandled stack trace instead of the script's normal error reporting, and no record of any kind is written for a prediction that may still be billing. The finally block in main does clean up the upload, so the impact is a bad failure mode, not a leak.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the poll fetch, check poll.ok, and print a readable error (prediction id, status) before exiting non-zero.

findings.description: `figure()` escapes `src` but interpolates the caption (prediction_id, sizes, diagnostics) into the HTML unescaped; all values are currently machine-generated, but a malformed run record would render arbitrary markup into the sheet.
findings.suggestion: Apply `html.escape(caption)` (or escape the interpolated fields) in `figure()`.

findings.description: The 'Original' row's exposure diagnostics are computed on the ICC-converted sRGB pixels from `original_rgb()`, while the module docstring (and `measure-hue-shares.py`'s method definition) fixes diagnostics as 'the file's encoded values'. For tuning photos with embedded P3/Adobe RGB profiles, the original's V≥0.90 / any=255 / mean values are silently measured by a different method than the output rows they sit next to.
findings.suggestion: Either measure the original's encoded values (decode without the sRGB conversion for the diagnostic pass) or document in the docstring and the sheet caption that the original is diagnosed after sRGB conversion for comparability.

findings.description: `point_bilinear` implements hand-rolled sampling geometry (clip, floor, edge clamping at sw-1, round-half-up) and the script's own docstring records that the filter choice flips S17-04's clipRatio across the 0.005 guard (Cloud gamma 1.50 vs 1.10) — this function directly decides tuning values, yet no test pins even one known input/output pair or the 'small bright points survive' property it exists to provide.
findings.suggestion: Add a small test with a known source/size pair asserting exact output bytes, plus a synthetic bright-point case demonstrating the no-prefilter property, so a refactor cannot silently change the sampler.

findings.description: The docstring promises exit 1 with a diagnostic on an 'unexpected shape' comparison input, but `compare()` only guards a missing id in the download (`if (!b)`); `const a = base[id]` is read unguarded, so a baseline lacking one of the tuning ids crashes with a TypeError instead of the promised exit-1 message.
findings.suggestion: Add the symmetric `if (!a) { console.error(id + ': missing from ' + baselinePath); process.exit(1); }` before computing `autoA`/`sideA`.

findings.description: ROI coordinates are floored with no clamping or emptiness check; a small ROI on a small image can produce `right == left`, so `pct` returns 0.0 but `mean` becomes NaN and prints `mean RGB nan nan nan` — silently useless output from a script whose selling point is reproducible numbers.
findings.suggestion: Guard `right > left and bottom > top` (and optionally validate the ROI against the manifest's roi_convention) before slicing.

findings.description: `figure()` escapes `src` but the captions interpolate `record['prediction_id']`, sizes and entry data into HTML unescaped. Values come from Replicate and the frozen manifest so the practical risk is nil, but the mixed escaping discipline invites injection the moment someone adds a free-form field to a run record.
findings.suggestion: Escape all interpolated caption values with `html.escape()` (or build captions from escaped parts consistently).

findings.description: `point_bilinear` is intricate numerical code whose stated purpose is to match Chromium's canvas sampler within one 1/255 bin — it directly guards the S17-04 clipRatio boundary that flips Cloud gamma 1.10↔1.50 — yet it has no unit test; parity is validated only by the ad-hoc browser-stats run requiring Playwright and the licensed photos. Similarly `exposure_stats`' V≥0.90/any=255 conventions in measure-hue-shares.py are untested.
findings.suggestion: Add a table-driven test with synthetic inputs (known 2×2 taps, rounding at exactly .5, degenerate 1-px dimensions, upscale case) pinning the sampler's contract cheaply.

findings.description: In `compare`, `b` (new download) is checked for presence but `a = base[id]` is not; a baseline missing a tuning id makes `auto(a)` throw a TypeError instead of the documented exit status 1 for unexpected shapes.
findings.suggestion: Add a symmetric check: `if (!a) { console.error(`${id}: missing from baseline`); process.exit(1); }`.

findings.description: The licensed-photo loading loop runs at module top level (lines 143-150, with a `throw` on hash mismatch) before `argv` is inspected for `--compare` (152-154). `--compare` is an offline analysis of a download against a baseline, but on a machine without the private `test-photos` it crashes with an unhandled ENOENT/throw instead of running the comparison.
findings.suggestion: Handle `--compare` before loading the photos, and make the manifest-mismatch path `process.exit(1)` rather than `throw`.

findings.description: When an upload succeeds but the response lacks `urls.get`, `localInput` exits before the `ImageInput` is constructed, so the `finally` in `main` never deletes `file.id` — the uploaded input leaks in the Replicate account despite the documented cleanup-after-run promise. The same holds for any throw between upload success and the try/finally.
findings.suggestion: Attempt the delete (or at least always report the file id as the exit does) inside a try/finally scoped around post-upload handling, e.g. catch the no-URL case, call deleteUpload with a synthesized ImageInput, then exit.

findings.description: Every photo is served with contentType "image/jpeg" regardless of its actual format. Browser sniffing usually saves this, but the harness's whole purpose is byte-reproducible browser decoding; a declared-correct content type is the safer guarantee.
findings.suggestion: Serve the content type from the manifest entry's file extension (or detect from magic bytes).

findings.description: collect() globs only `*.png.json`, but bread-spike.ts derives the sidecar filename from `extname(new URL(url).pathname) || ".png"`, so a non-PNG model output produces e.g. `<id>.jpg.json`, which the glob silently never matches. The run then vanishes from the contact sheet with no foreign/skip note — a calibration input can go missing without any signal.
findings.suggestion: Glob `*.json` in collect() (filtering by record shape / input_sha256 presence), or pin the sidecar extension to `.png` in the spike writer.

findings.description: build_photo opens every run output image simultaneously (`[(r, Image.open(...)) for r in runs]`) and keeps the file handles open through the whole sheet build. Fine for tens of runs, wasteful and fd-risky for larger sweeps.
findings.suggestion: Load each image eagerly (`.load()`/copy) and close it, or open inside a `with` at point of use.

findings.description: The documented exit contract promises 1 on an unexpected shape, but if the baseline lacks an id, `const a = base[id]` is undefined and `auto(a)` / `a.clipRatio` throws an unhandled TypeError, crashing with a stack trace and exit code 1 from the runtime rather than the intended clean error message (or worse, masking the real problem).
findings.suggestion: Guard `base[id]` (and missing fields in the legacy bare-object baseline shape) and `process.exit(1)` with a clear message, matching the docstring's contract.

findings.description: The comment says the uploaded file is deleted "only after the output is saved", but the finally block also runs when runPrediction returns early (create failed) or throws mid-poll, deleting the uploaded input while the prediction may still be non-terminal. Harmless in practice (a created prediction retains its input), but the comment overstates the guarantee.
findings.suggestion: Reword the comment to "best effort, after the run reaches its end" or restrict deletion to terminal-and-saved paths.

findings.description: A failed output download in saveOutput logs the error and returns without setting process.exitCode, so the script exits 0 after a paid prediction whose only artifact is the (expiring) Replicate output URL. Every other failure path in the script exits non-zero.
findings.suggestion: Set process.exitCode = 1 before returning from the !res.ok branch in saveOutput.

findings.description: `original.resize(target, Image.LANCZOS)` can upscale the original when it is smaller than the smallest output, breaking the docstring's matched-size contract ('An output is never enlarged; ... all are downscaled to the smallest') and the per-page 'every image at W×H' caption for the original figure.
findings.suggestion: Guard with a conditional resize and a visible note (like the differing-output-sizes note) when the original must be enlarged, or explicitly document that the original may be upscaled.

findings.description: point_bilinear — a hand-rolled canvas-emulating resampler whose rounding/support details directly move clipRatio across the 0.005 guard (per the module docstring) — has no automated tests, despite this PR existing because unreproducible numbers burned the team. Same for exposure_stats in scripts/measure-hue-shares.py (lines 124-129), whose denominators and thresholds are easy to silently regress.
findings.suggestion: Add small golden tests against fixed arrays (e.g. a known 4x4→2x2 point_bilinear case with the half-up rounding, an all-255 region asserting any=255 = 100%). They pin the method cheaply and match the repo's risk-weighted testing bar.

findings.description: compare() validates that the download contains each tuning id, but never checks the baseline side. With an old/partial baseline or a user-supplied --baseline file, `base[id]` is undefined and `auto(a)` / `a.clipRatio` throws a raw TypeError instead of the documented clean exit-1 'comparison could not run' path.
findings.suggestion: Add a mirrored `if (!a) { console.error(...); process.exit(1); }` check next to the existing `!b` check.

findings.description: `run.imageLabel.startsWith("data:") ? "(data URI)" : run.imageLabel` is dead code: imageLabel is `localPath ?? input.image`, so it is either a filesystem path or a remote URL, never a `data:` string. The guard implies a distinction that cannot occur.
findings.suggestion: Drop the ternary and record the label (or transport) directly.

findings.description: The run-record sidecar stores `output_file: dest` as an absolute OS-temp path. Once outputs are moved into the run directories contact-sheet.py scans (the documented workflow), that path is stale and misleading.
findings.suggestion: Drop the field or note in the header comment that it records the location at run time only; the sha256s are the durable identifiers.

note: counter delta exceeds the reported $0.000000 by $0.228943 (unreported spend, e.g. grading or an aborted request)

findings.description: Imports use ../../src/lib/... rather than the @/* alias mandated by repo rules; the same pattern appears in browser-stats.ts, desktop-stats.ts, and harness.ts. If scripts/ is intentionally outside the tsconfig alias scope these files also escape the root tsc/eslint graph, so typos (e.g. a missing LumaStats field) surface only at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Either include scripts/ in the alias/tsconfig scope, or add a header note stating how these files are type-checked (e.g. 'run npx tsx, not in the root tsc graph').

findings.description: collect() discovers run records via d.glob("*.png.json"), but bread-spike.ts writes its sidecar as `${dest}.json` where dest's extension comes from the output URL pathname — which may be .jpg, .webp, etc., not only .png. A run with a non-PNG-named output is silently invisible on the sheet instead of being reported, undercutting the documented 'exit 1 on a missing output' guarantee.
findings.suggestion: Either glob *.json and filter to records with a sibling image file, or pin the sidecar suffix to .png.json in bread-spike.ts so the two scripts agree.

findings.description: figure() HTML-escapes src but interpolates caption raw. Captions contain manifest paths and prediction_ids from run records (self-generated, so risk is low), but escaping the caption makes the invariant uniform and costs nothing.
findings.suggestion: Apply html.escape(caption) inside figure(), or escape the interpolated fragments at each call site.

findings.description: compare() assumes base[id] exists for every tuning entry. If the baseline file is stale and missing one of the six ids, auto(a) throws an unhandled TypeError instead of the documented 'exit 1: the comparison could not run' behaviour. Ids present in the baseline but absent from entries are also silently ignored.
findings.suggestion: Guard the missing-id case (and optionally the extra-id case), printing a message naming the id and file before process.exit(1).

findings.description: The sidecar guard run.imageLabel.startsWith("data:") is dead code: for local inputs imageLabel is always localPath (never the data URI), so the "(data URI)" branch can never fire. It happens to be harmless — recording the local path is more useful — but the condition suggests an intent the code doesn't have.
findings.suggestion: Simplify to input: run.imageLabel (or record the transport field, which already conveys data-uri vs upload vs url).

findings.description: manifest_roi does `entry["diagnostic_content_roi"]` without checking the key; a manifest entry lacking that field raises an unhelpful KeyError, at odds with the script's own fail-loudly-with-a-reason ethos. This is also the third independent loader of the s17-benchmark.json schema (here, contact-sheet.py, and s17/harness.ts), so a manifest schema change must be replicated in all three.
findings.suggestion: Check the field and `sys.exit` with an error naming the id and missing field; consider a single shared manifest loader if the schema is expected to evolve.

findings.description: A failure inside `page.evaluate` (fetch 404, decode failure) rejects the promise, so the script exits via unhandled rejection with a stack trace rather than the tidy status-1 "the check could not run" the docstring promises. The exit code coincidentally matches; the output does not.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the per-entry evaluate in try/catch, print a one-line reason, and `process.exit(1)`.

findings.description: `figure()` escapes `src` but interpolates `caption` unescaped into HTML; `prediction_id` is third-party API data flowing into the caption. Not exploitable here (local, trusted run records), but escaping costs nothing.
findings.suggestion: Apply `html.escape(caption)` (or escape the interpolated fields) in figure().

findings.description: build_photo computes exposure_stats twice per output image — once via `diagnostics()` and again for the markdown row — over full-resolution arrays.
findings.suggestion: Have diagnostics() return the raw values and reuse them in the markdown branch.

findings.description: In compare(), `const a = base[id]` is used without a presence check — only the download side (`b`) is validated. A baseline that predates a tuning id (or an older bare `{ id: stats }` baseline missing an entry) crashes with a raw TypeError from `auto(undefined)` instead of the documented "exit 1, comparison could not run" path.
findings.suggestion: Mirror the `!b` check: `if (!a) { console.error(`${id}: missing from baseline ${baselinePath}`); process.exit(1); }`

findings.description: The sidecar's `input: run.imageLabel.startsWith("data:") ? "(data URI)" : run.imageLabel` is a dead branch: `imageLabel` is the local file path for local inputs (the data URI lives in `input.image`), so the `"(data URI)"` arm is unreachable and misleadingly suggests inline inputs are redacted when they are recorded in full. The sidecar otherwise correctly records `input_sha256`, which contact-sheet.py relies on.
findings.suggestion: Drop the ternary and record a stable field, e.g. base `input` on `run.input.transport` ("data-uri"/"upload"/"url") or keep the path plus the input_sha256 that downstream consumers key on.

findings.description: `STAT_FIELDS`/`FIELDS`, the `PERCENTILES` set, and the tolerance/bin-rounding logic are duplicated between `browser-stats.ts` and `desktop-stats.ts`; the two will drift when the LumaStats shape or a threshold changes.
findings.suggestion: Move the field list and percentile set into `scripts/s17/harness.ts` next to the existing shared record shapes.

findings.description: `original.resize(target, ...)` forces the original into the exact pixel box of the smallest Bread output. The `note` on line 143 only fires when outputs differ from each other; if a single output's aspect ratio differs from the source's, the original is silently distorted on the sheet the maintainer tunes from — the artifact where aspect distortion is most misleading.
findings.suggestion: Compare the original's aspect ratio to `target`; on mismatch either letterbox or print a warning alongside the existing size note.

findings.description: `point_bilinear` (and the jpeg-draft pipeline around it) hand-reproduces Chromium's `drawImage` sampler, including floor-half-up rounding. The docstring itself records that small sampler differences flipped S17-04 across the 0.005 clip guard (Cloud gamma 1.50 vs 1.10). This is exactly the kind of fragile numeric behavior that deserves a golden test, yet the diff adds none — a future cleanup of the rounding or a Pillow drift would go unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Add a small golden-pixel test: a stored small source image plus expected sampled output array (captured from a verified run), asserted against `point_bilinear` and the jpeg-draft path.

findings.description: `compare()` verifies each baseline id exists in the download, but not the reverse: if the baseline lacks an id, `a` is `undefined` and `auto(a)` throws a TypeError instead of exiting 1 with a message naming the id — violating the tool's own exit-status contract (1 = comparison could not run).
findings.suggestion: Check `if (!a) { console.error(`${id}: missing from ${baselinePath}`); process.exit(1); }` before calling `auto(a)`.

findings.description: `--compare` mode is dispatched at module scope (line 155), but lines 145–150 already read and hash every licensed tuning photo at load time and throw on mismatch or missing files. Since `test-photos/private/` is gitignored, `--compare <download.json>` on any machine without the inputs dies with an unhandled throw instead of the documented "exit 1, comparison could not run" behavior.
findings.suggestion: Move the photo loading loop after the `--compare` dispatch (or gate it behind a `serve` code path) so compare mode needs only the baseline and download files.

findings.description: `run.imageLabel.startsWith("data:")` is dead code: `imageLabel` is always the local path or a remote URL, never a data URI, so the ternary's first branch can never be taken.
findings.suggestion: Drop the ternary and record `run.imageLabel` directly (the local path is the more useful record anyway).

findings.description: The exposure method documentation says the ROI is interpreted 'per the manifest's roi_convention', but exposure() (lines 140-152) never reads that field — it unconditionally treats diagnostic_content_roi as normalized [left, top, right, bottom]. If the manifest ever carries a different convention, the printed numbers silently change meaning while the docstring claims the convention is honoured.
findings.suggestion: Either read and honour roi_convention in manifest_roi()/exposure(), or drop the claim from the docstring and state that the ROI is always normalized ltrb.

findings.description: The docstring claims the sample sides use 'the client's own arithmetic', but Python's round() uses banker's rounding while JS Math.round() rounds half away from zero. When w*scale lands exactly on .5 the offline sample is one pixel off the browser's, shifting every downstream LumaStats field for that photo — precisely the drift this harness exists to catch. point_bilinear() already rounds half-up correctly; this is the one spot that doesn't.
findings.suggestion: Use half-up rounding to match JS: `max(1, math.floor(w * scale + 0.5))` (and likewise for sh).

findings.description: compare() validates that the download has an entry for each tuning id (exits 1 with a clean message) but reads the baseline entry with no such guard: `const a = base[id]` is passed straight into auto(a). If the pinned baseline — or an older-format --baseline file, which readStats explicitly accepts — lacks a tuning id, the tool crashes with an unhandled TypeError instead of the documented exit-1 path.
findings.suggestion: Mirror the download guard: `const a = base[id]; if (!a) { console.error(`${id}: missing from ${baselinePath}`); process.exit(1); }`

findings.description: `input: run.imageLabel.startsWith("data:") ? "(data URI)" : run.imageLabel` is dead code: for local files imageLabel is the file path, never the data URI (that lives in input.image). The guard can never fire, and it suggests a redaction that isn't actually there.
findings.suggestion: Drop the conditional and record imageLabel (or the transport field) directly — the sidecar already captures the transport separately.
